title: Send new consignment orders from Dataverse to SAP automatically
summary: When someone creates a consignment order, it is created in SAP for them, the product's translations are copied back, and the order is marked Synced.

requirements.text: Start when someone creates a consignment order from a work order in Dataverse
Check that all needed information is there before calling SAP
Convert the order into SAP's format
Find which languages the product has in SAP
Copy translations only for languages Dataverse also has; skip the rest
A few orders a day, one at a time
requirements.note: Tell us if this is wrong

outcomes: An order with missing information never reaches SAP. You see the reason on the order.
"Synced" appears only when SAP has confirmed the order and every translation was saved.
Only languages in both systems get a translation. Skipped languages are listed with a reason.
Running it twice never creates a second SAP order or duplicate translations.
example: SAP has English, German, French and Polish. Dataverse has English, German, French and Dutch. Result: 3 translations created, Polish skipped, order marked Synced.

steps.title: You create a consignment order
steps.text: From a work order in Dataverse, as you do today.

steps.title: We check nothing is missing
steps.text: If something is missing, you see a clear message on the order.

steps.title: We create it in SAP and double-check
steps.text: We confirm SAP really saved it before moving on.

steps.title: We copy the product's translations
steps.text: Only for languages both systems use.

steps.title: The order is marked "Synced"
steps.text: Only when every step above worked.

suggestion: Keep it simple. One Azure Logic App runs all five steps. We'll only add more pieces if your answers show we need them.

main.name: Dataverse
main.text: Consignment order and its product translations

main.name: Logic App
main.text: One automated workflow: check, create in SAP, copy translations, mark Synced

main.name: SAP
main.text: Creates the consignment and holds product texts

flow.text: Dataverse sends the new order to the workflow.
The workflow creates the consignment in SAP.
SAP confirms it and returns the product's translations.
Matching translations are saved and the order is marked Synced.

architecture.note: All SAP traffic goes through the secure connection.

key_rule.title: The language rule

items.label: Ignored
items.text: Dutch (SAP has no Dutch text for this product)

key_rule.note: If a language could match two options (for example English to US or UK), we don't guess; a person checks it. If no languages match at all, the order shows Needs checking instead of Synced.

protections.title: No duplicate orders
protections.text: If the flow runs twice, SAP still gets only one order.

protections.title: No false "success"
protections.text: SAP can say OK with warnings and still not save. We read the order back to be sure.

protections.title: No endless loops
protections.text: When we mark the order Synced, that change won't start the flow again.

protections.title: Problems are visible
protections.text: If anything is unsure, the order says Needs checking instead of failing silently.

questions.title: How does SAP accept a new consignment order?
questions.why: We have to send orders in exactly the format SAP expects, or SAP rejects them.
questions.tech: WSDL/XSD, BAPI/RFC name, IDoc type or OData service for create and for reading product texts; one or several product lines?

questions.title: How can we be sure SAP really saved the order?
questions.why: SAP can reply OK and still not save it. Checking stops lost or doubled orders.
questions.tech: Commit behaviour and read-back operation; can SAP store the Dataverse ID as an external reference?

questions.title: Where are the languages kept in Dataverse?
questions.why: To match languages correctly. For example, SAP calls German D and Dataverse calls it 1031.
questions.tech: Provisioned LCIDs or custom table; SPRAS/LAISO to Dataverse mapping; table and key column names

questions.title: Should the user wait for SAP, or just see a status?
questions.why: SAP can be slow. Showing a status (Processing, then Synced) avoids timeouts.
questions.tech: Trigger type (Power Automate, plugin/webhook or Dataverse connector) and required fields

questions.title: Where does your SAP system run?
questions.why: This decides how Azure can reach SAP safely, and it affects cost.
questions.tech: On-premises data gateway or VNet; Logic Apps Consumption or Standard; identity for Dataverse

requirements.text: Dataverse calls the Logic App when a consignment order is created
Translations only for SAP and active Dataverse languages

steps: Trigger with a status gate (only when Submitted) to prevent loops.
Validate required fields; on failure write the reason and set Failed.
Idempotency check: existing SAP number or pending state?
SAP create: check RETURN and warnings, commit, read back; uncertain means NeedsVerification.
Intersect languages through one confirmed mapping; quarantine ambiguous matches.
Upsert translations keyed by consignment + language; set Synced only if SAP and all translations succeeded.
notes: Alternative: add an Azure Function for mapping if the rules get complex.
Not recommended yet: Service Bus, unless long SAP outages or large peaks must be absorbed.
